episode_title: Optimizing IoT Data Transmission with Charles Yeomans of AtomBeam Technologies

real_qa.q: How much IoT data is projected to be generated globally in 2025 according to IDC?
real_qa.r: According to IDC, in 2025 there will be about 90 zettabytes generated by IoT. To give scale, if you add up all the storage capacity of all data centers in the world, it's about two zettabytes, showing a massive difference between data generated and capacity to store or transmit it.

real_qa.q: What data reduction percentage does AtomBeam Technologies achieve with its pattern-matching compression technology?
real_qa.r: AtomBeam achieves about 75% smaller overall datagrams on average, doing it in microseconds, which results in moving four times more data over the same network pipe. The technology uses machine learning to build a codebook in a couple of minutes by identifying repeating bit patterns in IoT payloads.

real_qa.q: How many patents does AtomBeam Technologies currently hold and have pending?
real_qa.r: AtomBeam has 36 patents so far and another 40 more pending, reflecting the company's multidisciplinary approach to protecting its fundamental technology innovation in IoT data transmission.

real_qa.q: How much has AtomBeam raised through crowdfunding on StartEngine under Regulation CF and Reg A+?
real_qa.r: AtomBeam has raised 8.5 million dollars on StartEngine so far. In the most recent round closed in December, seeking 2 million, they maxed out at 3.3 million under Reg A+ regulations, with an additional 3.6 million on the waitlist they could not accept.

real_qa.q: What is Link 16 and what bandwidth limitations does the U.S. military face with this technology?
real_qa.r: Link 16 is 1980s technology that serves as the main backbone for DoD communications with bandwidth of either 57 kilobits per second or 111 kilobits per second. This creates a significant bottleneck where 21st century military aircraft generating gigabits of data must squeeze that information down to send over a pipe with only 57 kilobits capacity.

real_qa.q: What is the acoustic data transmission rate for underwater communications according to the episode?
real_qa.r: Underwater acoustic data transmission is severely limited at 44 bits per second—not kilobits or gigabits—which creates an extreme challenge for naval systems trying to send images and real-time data from submarines and underwater operations.
real_qa.requete: underwater acoustic transmission 44 bits per second

guest.bio_context: Charles Yeomans is a former Navy intelligence officer with an MBA from Stanford who has held multiple executive roles including COO of an insurance broker, CEO of a benefits enrollment platform company, and CEO of a biotech venture in Chile. He has extensive experience in Wall Street finance, management, and technology ventures, and founded AtomBeam Technologies after recognizing a fundamental technological gap in IoT data transmission that patent lawyers confirmed was a clear, unprotected field.
